newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's central bank downgrades 1997 growth.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's central bank downgrades 1997 growth.

text.p: Ecuador's Central Bank said Thursday it has downgraded its 1997 gross domestic product growth forecast to 3.3 percent from 3.5 percent.
At the same time it upgraded its estimate for 1998 growth to 4.3 percent from 4.0 percent.
"This growth will be driven mainly by an increase in investment by public and private companies," said the central bank in a statement.
The government forecast in February that growth in 1997 will be 3.5 percent and in 1998 it will rise to 4.0 percent. Last year growth dipped to 2.0 percent because of a slowdown in the oil industry.
In 1997 the oil sector will expand 4.6 percent while the manufacturing, transport and communications industries will grow 3.2 percent, the central bank predicted.
In 1998 it saw the oil sector picking up sharply to register 14.2 percent growth.
Oil production is seen rising to 158.8 million barrels in 1998 from 145.6 million barrels this year, said the central bank.
Petroleum exports are the main source of foreign currency for Ecuador and make up about 50 percent of the government's annual revenues.
